A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 53-page versions of Relational Structural Causal Models with matching main sections and Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment; the appendices are identical.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original traffic-simulation results for RNCM estimation, identification, scalability, and sensitivity to misspecified assumptions.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain these original simulation results, including front-door estimation and graph/aggregator misspecification experiments.

M1.justification: The RSCM and RNCM definitions, shared mechanisms, training objectives, and identification/estimation procedures in Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same simulated traffic scenarios, source/target skeletons, causal queries, larger relational structures, and misspecification conditions in Section 6 and Appendix E.

E2.justification: The estimation comparison retains NCM-X, NCM-J, REL-MLP, REL-MLP + DEG, and the target-trained NCM*. The graph-misspecification comparison also retains the same flat NCM baselines.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, source/target configurations, evaluation metrics, data generation, model architecture, and training settings are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same experiment-specific protocols.

E4.justification: The source-neighborhood analysis in Section 6.1, scalability/runtime study in E.7, and graph/aggregator misspecification analyses in E.8 are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Seed/trial descriptions and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including Figure 4's 25th–75th percentile bands across 10 seeds and E.5's five-trial estimate.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted rankings and trends, and qualitative findings match. For example, E.5 reports the same front-door MSE of 0.00082 ± 0.0018, and Figures 3–4 and the appendix result figures are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, identification and expressivity results, and appendix proofs are unchanged. Restoring missing closing parentheses in Section 6.1's probability expression is a typesetting correction.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same claims. The revised conclusion explicitly mentions observational distributions of unseen object combinations, already covered by v1's abstract, introduction, and theory.

C2.justification: Interpretations of generalization, identifiability, scalability, and misspecification remain unchanged. Appendix F retains the same qualifications about required structural knowledge, aggregation costs, and discrete neural implementations.

D1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit pointer to the CausalAILab/RelationalCausalModels code repository, absent from v1. Implementation, hardware, data-generation, and training details in E.1–E.3 remain unchanged; the PDFs establish the new access information, not repository contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including Appendix A. Reference-list differences are line wrapping rather than additions or removals.

P1.justification: The conclusion is lightly rephrased, acknowledgements add thanks to anonymous reviewers, publication metadata is added, and two missing probability-expression parentheses are corrected. The section organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The added proceedings/copyright footer and short textual additions cause limited column and page reflow, including in the references. Figures, tables, axes, legends, and captions retain the same content and structure.

improvement.justification: The new implementation-repository pointer improves reproducibility documentation, while the punctuation fixes and revised conclusion modestly improve clarity. These are limited gains; the methods, theoretical support, experiments, and appendices remain unchanged.
